Hi Priyom,

Attached is PayCore's Q3 usage export for the period Jul 1–Sep 30. We ran into a couple of unexpected spikes in August (marketing experiment + AI fraud detection pilot) and it looks like we exceeded our committed monthly capacity in two separate weeks. The file includes per-route token counts and peak concurrency times.

Quick ask: can Redwood confirm whether the excess should be treated as billable overage or if it qualifies for a one-time true-up given the upgrade we executed mid-quarter? Procurement has asked for a single one-time invoice to reconcile the delta if possible.

Attachments: paycore-q3-usage-breakdown.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

Jordan — thanks for the data. I pulled the CSV and started an initial pass. Two quick notes:

- The mid-quarter upgrade (2026-08-12) changed your committed vCPU/GPU backing for the route (you migrated from shared to Dedicated-2 pool), which affects how excess tokens are priced versus earlier in the quarter.
- We do allow a retroactive true-up as a one-time settlement in cases where the customer upgraded during the quarter and the usage deltas look like a migration spike rather than sustained overages.

Looping in Monica and Vivek from Billing/Contracts so we can propose the final $ amount and invoice mechanics. Monica — can you confirm if we can apply a pro-rated commitment adjustment and a single invoice for the delta? Vivek — any constraints on how we record this for ARR and reporting?

I'll pull a quick estimate and send a proposed settlement table by EOD Fri.

Cheers,
Priyom
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q3 usage reconciliation - initial figures

Internal — I reviewed the usage CSV and the commit/upgrade timeline. My proposed approach:

1) Calculate the delta between what PayCore would have paid under their original commit vs actual consumption for 7/1–8/11 (pre-upgrade) and 8/12–9/30 (post-upgrade) with the post-upgrade dedicated pricing applied to post-upgrade usage.
2) If > 10% of quarter spend is attributable to migration-related burst patterns (which it is), offer a one-time true-up invoice covering the delta instead of per-month overage billing.
3) Record the settlement as a one-time professional/invoice line (non-recurring) tied to DEAL-5843 and include an explicit note in the contract amendment that future overages revert to standard per-token billing.

Estimated one-time amount (preliminary): $24,500 — this is conservative and assumes 20% of the observed excess is migration noise.

I'll attach a reconciliation workbook and a draft invoice for review. Priyom — please share this with Jordan + procurement and ask for sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-settlement-proposal-DEAL-5843.xlsx

Thanks — Monica
Sr. Revenue Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@paycore.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0700

Monica — appreciate the quick analysis. PayCore is good with a one-time invoice if the settlement covers the full delta and we receive the final invoice and brief amendment to the SOW. Procurement prefers a single charge rather than retro monthly invoices.

Two asks: can you include a short note stating this is a one-time settlement tied to the migration activity (so our accounting treats it as a one-off), and provide the DocuSign link for the amendment? We can get this through legal + finance quickly if that's included.

If $24.5k is the number, we can approve for payment on receipt of the invoice.

— Jordan
